title: The Ethics of the Humblebrag
script: Rafi: [thoughtful] You posted about the food drive again. Third time this month, if I'm counting correctly.
Nadia: The point is to encourage others to donate, not to advertise myself, if that's the accusation you're circling toward.
Rafi: [carefully] Fair enough, but does the caption need your own hands in the photo, reaching toward the camera rather than the recipient?
Nadia: I hadn't consciously framed it that way, though now that you mention it, I can't entirely defend the composition.
Rafi: [reflective] I'm not accusing you of anything cynical. I think the instinct to be seen doing good is nearly universal, and resisting it entirely might be an unrealistic standard.
Nadia: So where do you draw the line between mobilizing people and simply performing for them?
Rafi: [honestly] Perhaps the test isn't whether anyone sees it, but whether you'd still do it exactly the same way if no one ever would.
Nadia: By that measure, wouldn't almost any organized charity fail? Fundraisers depend on visibility; anonymity doesn't scale the way discretion might prefer.
Rafi: [gently] That's a legitimate objection. Visibility can serve the cause even while quietly flattering the person behind it, and untangling the two motives is genuinely difficult.
Nadia: So what would you have me do, delete the account and mail cash to strangers in unmarked envelopes?
Rafi: [calmly] Not necessarily, though there's a certain elegance to that image. I'd just suggest interrogating the caption before you write it, not after someone else questions it.
Nadia: Ask myself whether I'm documenting the drive or documenting my participation in it, you mean.
Rafi: [encouraging] Exactly that distinction. One serves the recipients; the other quietly serves you while borrowing their need as its backdrop.
Nadia: That's an uncomfortably precise way of putting it, and I suspect it applies to more of my posts than I'd like to admit.
Rafi: [seriously] For what it's worth, the drive itself is good regardless. I'm only asking you to keep watching the seam where generosity and self-image start to overlap.
Nadia: Next post, no photo of me at all. Just the address, the need, and nothing performed in between.

quiz.question: What does Rafi notice about Nadia's recent posts?
options: Three food-drive posts with her own hands in the photos.
She never posts about charity
She deleted her account
She only posts anonymously
quiz.explanation: Rafi points out this is the third post this month, and questions why her own hands appear reaching toward the camera.

quiz.question: What test does Rafi propose for distinguishing sincere action from performance?
options: Whether the act raises money
Whether it gets likes
Whether you'd still do it exactly the same way if no one would ever see it
Whether a charity organizes it
quiz.explanation: Rafi suggests the test is whether one would act the same way even if no one would ever witness it.

quiz.question: What objection does Nadia raise about that test?
options: That it's too easy to pass
That almost any organized charity would fail it, since fundraisers depend on visibility
That anonymity is always better
That Rafi doesn't understand charity work
quiz.explanation: Nadia argues that fundraisers depend on visibility to scale, so the test would condemn most organized charity.

quiz.question: What distinction does Rafi ask Nadia to interrogate?
options: Whether to donate money or food
Whether to post in the morning or evening
Whether her friends approve
Whether a post documents the drive itself or documents her participation in it
quiz.explanation: He asks her to distinguish between documenting the cause versus documenting her own involvement in it.

quiz.question: What does Nadia decide for her next post?
options: To stop posting about charity entirely
To post more photos of herself
To make the account private
To post only the address and the need, without any photo of herself
quiz.explanation: Nadia resolves that her next post will include only the address and the need, with no photo of herself.

quiz.question: What distinction guides Nadia's next post?
options: Whether it centres recipients' needs rather than her participation.
Whether it gets the most likes.
Whether Rafi approves it.
Whether it includes a confession.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: Why reject a ban on visible charity?
options: Visibility always proves insincerity.
Visibility can mobilise support while motives still need examination.
Anonymous gifts are the only valid ones.
Fundraisers cannot benefit recipients.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: What does Rafi's test examine?
options: Whether the photo is well framed.
Whether donors praise the organiser.
Whether the action would remain unchanged without an audience.
Whether donations arrive quickly.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: How should Nadia treat the tension?
options: As a mixed-motive problem requiring honest self-questioning.
As proof she must close the drive.
As irrelevant because the cause is good.
As a problem for followers alone.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.

quiz.question: Which revision applies their discussion?
options: Add a longer story of sacrifice.
Post the address and need without centring herself.
Ask donors to praise volunteers.
Replace the drive with secrecy.
quiz.explanation: The audio supports this interpretation of its central argument.
